claim: The Minett Trail is a ~90 km hiking route split into 10 station-to-station stages crossing the Pro-Sud municipalities, with stages ranging 6–16 km (e.g. Belval–Esch 6.5 km, Pétange–Differdange 15.7 km).
quote: Clemency to Pétange: 7.2 km; Pétange to Differdange: 15.7 km; Differdange to Belvaux: 8.15 km; Belvaux to Esch-sur-Alzette: 6.5 km; Esch-sur-Alzette to Tétange: 11.95 km; Rumelange to Dudelange: 10.9 km

claim: The Minett region was granted UNESCO Man and Biosphere reserve status in October 2020 and the trail features 11 architect-designed 'Kabaisercher' overnight lodges including a floating lodge on a Dudelange lake and a repurposed railway carriage at Fond-de-Gras.
quote: In October of 2020, the Minett region became a biosphere reserve recognised by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO). Eleven different unforgettable accommodations called Kabaisercher

claim: The Ellergronn nature reserve in Esch-sur-Alzette (Rue Jean-Pierre Bausch) is a former iron-ore mining site now part of Natura 2000, with a Centre Nature et Forêt visitor centre and trails including a Norbert Theis nature path and the Natura 2000 trail.
quote: Rue Jean-Pierre Bausch, L-4114 Esch-sur-Alzette ... ponds and the dry grass so typical of the region, on the edge of an alder and ash forest ... designated as part of Natura 2000

claim: The Ellergronn Loop is roughly 5 km (3 mi) with about 130 m (423 ft) elevation gain and is rated moderate, taking about 1 h 18 min on average.
quote: The Ellergronn Loop is a trail located in Réserve naturelle Ellergronn, covering 3 miles with an elevation gain of 423 ft near Esch-sur-Alzette. It's generally considered a moderately challenging route that takes an average of 1 hour 18 minutes

claim: Prënzebierg–Giele Botter (rue Titelberg, Differdange) is a former open-pit mine reclaimed by nature, hosting wild orchids, bats and amphibians, with several waymarked trails including the Sentier géologique Giele Botter.
quote: formerly an open-pit mine ... wild orchids alongside amphibians, reptiles, insects, bats, and bird species ... Sentier géologique 'Giele Botter'

claim: Trail options at Prënzebierg–Giele Botter include the easy 4.1 km Auto-Pédestre Differdange (~1 h), the moderate 2.4 km Geological Trail Giele Botter (~45 min), and the moderate 7.6 km Discovery Trail with 230 m ascent (~2 h 15).
quote: Auto-Pédestre Differdange: An easy hiking round trip that is 4.1 km ... Geological Trail 'Giele Botter': A moderate difficulty geological trail of 2.4 km ... Discovery Trail: A moderate difficulty hike of 7.6 km lasting 2:15 hours with 230 m ascent

claim: The PC3 Piste cyclable des Trois Rivières runs 90.3 km from Schengen along the Moselle to Wasserbillig, then up the Sûre to Reisdorf and the Our to Vianden, partly on disused railway lines.
quote: 90,30 km ... The path follows three river systems: the Moselle (Schengen to Wasserbillig), the Sauer (Wasserbillig to Reisdorf), and the Our (Reisdorf to Vianden) ... partly on old railway tracks

claim: The Moselle section of PC3 around Remich is flat and considered ideal for beginners or relaxed riding, and a round trip from Remich to Schengen is roughly 20 km.
quote: A detour to Schengen from Remich is about 20km round trip along the Moselle ... this flat route is perfect for beginners or those looking for a more relaxed ride

claim: The PC6 Piste cyclable des Trois Cantons is a 57.5 km medium-difficulty route with 343 m elevation gain linking Pétange to Remerschen via Sanem, Schifflange, Bettembourg, Altwies and Mondorf — passing close to Frisange.
quote: The PC6 (Trois Cantons cycle path) is 57,532 km long ... connects Pétange to Remerschen via Sanem, Schifflange, Bettembourg, Altwies and Mondorf ... altitude gain of 343 m and an estimated running time of 04h00 with medium difficulty

claim: The PC1 Piste cyclable du Centre is a 42.1 km loop around Luxembourg City with 412 m of climbing, starting at Kockelscheuer ponds and passing the Bockfelsen and Kirchberg.
quote: The PC1 (Centre) is a cycling route that covers a distance of 42.1 km with 412 m of ascent ... loop around the capital of the Grand Duchy ... starting at the Kockelscheuer site with its romantic ponds

claim: The Pétrusse Valley walk in Luxembourg City is about 5 km with ~150 m elevation, linking the Petruss banks to the Alzette around Clausen and back up via Pfaffenthal in 1.5–2 hours, considered moderate.
quote: The trail stretches roughly 5 kilometers with a moderate elevation gain of about 150 meters ... begins in the south-west on the Petruss ... reach the upper town via Pfaffenthal ... approximately 1.5–2 hr to complete

claim: Kockelscheuer south of Luxembourg City offers 16 hectares of park, ponds and forest with an 8.9 km circular trail and a fitness/parcours circuit, easily reached by bus 18 from Hamilius.
quote: 16 hectares of park, ponds and forest ... The 8.9 km long route starts at the ponds of Kockelscheuer, leading clockwise through the forest ... Bus line 18 (Kockelscheuer, Patinoire) from the Hamilius Quai 2 stop

claim: The Mondorf-les-Bains Loop is a ~10 km (6 mi) moderate hike with ~205 m (675 ft) elevation starting along the Gander stream, taking 2.5–3 hours; gentler nearby alternatives include the 7.4 km Mondorf–Ellange Loop (easy, ~1 h 47).
quote: Mondorf-les-Bains Loop ... covers 6 miles with an elevation gain of 675 feet. It takes about 2.5–3 hours ... Mondorf-Ellange Loop is a 4.6-mile loop trail considered an easy route that takes an average of 1 hour 47 minutes

claim: The Mullerthal Trail ('Little Switzerland') runs 112 km through eastern Luxembourg around Echternach, roughly 30 km from Luxembourg City — placing its core trailheads (Echternach, Berdorf, Consdorf) outside a 30 km radius of Frisange.
quote: The Mullerthal Trail leads over 112 kilometres through the fascinating scenic diversity of the Mullerthal Region - Luxembourg's Little Switzerland ... in the Eastern part of Luxembourg ... about 30 kilometers from Luxembourg City
